newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Aid groups suspend operations in western Liberia.
newsitem.headline: Aid groups suspend operations in western Liberia.

text.p: International aid groups suspended activities and withdrew from western Liberia's Grand Cape Mount county on Friday, citing harassment of personnel and worsening insecurity.

The U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs said in a statement that the decision was jointly taken by local and international aid groups after ULIMO-J rebel fighters repeatedly threatened and harassed aid workers and seized relief vehicles.
It cited an attack on a village in which four civilians suffered serious gunshot wounds on Thursday.

The aid groups said these incidents threatened the safety of aid workers and the civilian populations in territories controlled by the ULIMO-J faction led by ethnic Krahn clan leader General Roosevelt Johnson.

Disarmament of Liberia's rebel factions under a regional plan to end seven years of civil war is continuing across the West African country but the United Nations said on Thursday it was unimpressed with the slow pace of the exercise.
U.N. special envoy Anthony Nyakyi said the programme started well nearly a month ago but had slowed to a snail's pace.
"It was our hope that by now at least 20,000 combatants would have beem disarmed and demobilsed," Nyakyi said in a statement.

The West African peacekeeping force ECOMOG, striking a more upbeat note, says it has disarmed close to 5,000 guerrillas despite the failure of promised troop reinforcements from regional governments to arrive.
